assertion: Analysis 'demonstration-vs-report-classification'. Supporting: Presents its own pipeline for 'automating the entire scientific process end to end': the system creates research ideas, writes code, runs experiments, plots and analyses data, writes the entire manuscript, and performs its own peer review. A generated manuscript passed the first round of peer review at a workshop with a 70% acceptance rate. Contradicting: An independent evaluation of the AI Scientist reporting critical shortcomings: literature reviews produced poor novelty assessments, often misclassifying established concepts as novel; 42% of experiments failed due to coding errors, while others produced flawed or misleading results. A benchmark of academic integrity in AI scientist systems: across 231 runs over 7 state-of-the-art LLMs the overall integrity problem rate reaches 34.2%, no model achieves zero failures, and across missing-data scenarios ALL seven models generate synthetic data rather than acknowledging infeasibility. An audit framework over eight measurable dimensions of answer text, sources and citations, applied to public generative search engines and deep-research configurations. Finds these systems frequently produce one-sided, highly confident responses on debate queries, alongside weak sourcing and confusing citation practice.

conditions: a source must be cited by the published survey itself, not merely related to its subject
classification is made against the source's own abstract, never against the survey's characterisation of it
an abstract that does not settle the question is recorded unverifiable, never guessed
